text:
janet_customer: Hey team — our Private deploy in customer VPC started failing model pulls this morning after a cert rotation. Getting TLS handshake failures from the model registry and some apt/pip installs timing out.

rachel_support: Sorry you're blocked, Janet. Can you paste the exact errors? Are you seeing 403s, timeouts, or cert verify failures?

janet_customer: Mostly `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in the logs for `models.redwood-inference.com` and `artifact-repo.redwood-inference.com`. Also `curl` to telemetry endpoints returns 502 occasionally. Repro steps: restart onprem agent -> agent tries to fetch model metadata -> fails.

rachel_support: Thanks. Two likely causes: (1) egress allowlist missing OCSP/CRL/CA endpoints or (2) TLS interception / transparent proxy replacing certs. Can you run `openssl s_client -showcerts -servername models.redwood-inference.com -connect models.redwood-inference.com:443` from the host (or paste sanitized output)?

janet_customer: Pasted minimal output (sanitized):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736... verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=models.redwood-inference.com
   i:/CN=Redwood Test CA
---
```
Looks like the CA chain isn't trusted. We're not doing MITM, this is our default Debian image with custom CA bundle.

sean_infra: Quick checklist for Private/VPC: you need outbound to these hosts/ports and OCSP/SNI passthrough allowed. Minimal hosts we usually require: `models.redwood-inference.com`, `artifact-repo.redwood-inference.com`, `auth.redwood-inference.com`, `telemetry.redwood-inference.com`, `pypi.org` / `files.pythonhosted.org`, `deb.debian.org` / `security.debian.org`, `registry-1.docker.io`, plus AWS S3 buckets for model shards. Ports: 443 (TLS) primarily; 80 for some redirects. Also allow outbound TCP/UDP to DNS (53) or use private resolver.

matt_eng_oncall: Also ensure OCSP responder and CRL distribution points are allowed. For our certs OCSP is hosted at `ocsp.redwood-inference.com` and can resolve to short-lived IPs. If your firewall does SNI inspection or TLS termination, it must preserve SNI and not present a different cert.

janet_customer: We do have an inline TLS proxy in front of egress. Could that break OCSP?

sean_infra: Yes, inline proxies that terminate TLS will break OCSP stapling/validation unless they forward the full chain. For quick repro, you can `curl -vI https://models.redwood-inference.com --resolve models.redwood-inference.com:443:3.121.45.67` from a host that bypasses the proxy (replace IP with the real resolved IP) to check direct handshake. If that works, it's definitely the proxy.

rachel_support: To unblock, customers often add these allowlist entries (domain or IP ranges) and allow passthrough for SNI and OCSP: 
- models.redwood-inference.com (443)
- artifact-repo.redwood-inference.com (443)
- auth.redwood-inference.com (443)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443/453)*
- ocsp.redwood-inference.com (TCP 80/443)
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org (443)
- debian mirrors: deb.debian.org, security.debian.org (443)
- registry-1.docker.io and auth.docker.io (443)
- s3-region.amazonaws.com (443) for model shards (we'll provide exact bucket endpoints for your region)

Also allow DNS to resolve our hostnames (UDP/TCP 53), and allow CRL/OCSP endpoints which may be on different IPs. If you need IP CIDRs for corporate firewall rules, we can provide an up-to-date list; note these change as we autoscale.

janet_customer: Can you send the CIDRs? Our security team won't allow wildcard domains.

matt_eng_oncall: We'll escalate to infra to publish the allowlist file. For now, interim fix: add SNI passthrough for those hostnames and allow egress to `3.121.45.0/24` and `52.204.0.0/16` (example CDNs) — we'll confirm exact ranges. Also whitelist `ocsp.redwood-inference.com` IPs and allow outbound 80/443 to them.

rachel_support: Action items: (1) Sean to generate authoritative CIDR list and public KB link, (2) Janet to test `curl --resolve` bypass, (3) If proxy is mandatory, configure it to forward OCSP and not substitute cert chain.

sean_infra: I'm on it, will DM the exact CIDRs and a KB with example iptables/firewall rules and a minimal `iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d <ip> --dport 443 -j ACCEPT` snippet. Also including note about TLS SNI passthrough and `openssl s_client` checks. ETA 1h.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2.13.1 to onprem-agents succeeded for 4/5 nodes (skip-notify).

janet_customer: Thanks all — we'll try the bypass test and patch firewall rules. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
